# E057 -- 92NY (The 92nd Street Y)

## Metadata

- **Page count:** 39
- **Prepared by:** Pentagram

## Brand Strategy
- No explicit brand strategy section; the document is a visual identity system. Brand personality implied through design language: "sophistication," "confidence," "consistency."

## Logo
- "92NY" wordmark is the core mark.
- **Sub-brand lockup system:** "Center for [Name]" format using Theinhardt Pan Ultralight (tracked -20, leading 100%) at cap height of the wordmark.
- Sub-brands include: Center for Children & Family, Bronfman Center for Jewish Life, Center for the Arts, Belfer Center for Innovation & Social Impact, Center for Community, Donor Center for Name.
- **Logo Band system:** A strip of black or white positioned at the top of any application, holding the parent brand logo or sub-brand lockups. Rules: always top and left-aligned, tight spacing matching clearspace, clean line (no border/drop shadow), black and white only.

## Typography
- **Theinhardt Pan** (Ultralight weight visible in sub-brand lockups). Full typography section starts at page 16.

## Color
- **Primary palette:** Black and white (neutral). "When in doubt, black & white only."
- **Secondary palette** (5 colors, each with full HEX/RGB/CMYK/PMS specs):
  - Blue: #8eaae2 (PMS 292 C)
  - Green: #21805e (PMS 340C)
  - Pink: #edabba (PMS 182 C)
  - Magenta: #990d61 (PMS 676 C)
  - Red-orange: #ff5447 (PMS Warm Red C)
- **Color rules:** Strict -- one secondary color per application only; never mix secondary colors; lean into layering with black/white; equal distribution across all brand expressions (no color-coding by department).
- Described as "vibrant but sophisticated, idiosyncratic but pleasing."

## Graphics / Iconography
- The Logo Band is a distinctive graphic device -- a systematic framing element across all applications.
